terra.problem: Saying Moses and the elders belong to another Bible story makes a claim about Scripture outside this passage without a reference.
The psalm does not say the rulers want to be loud or that they plan not to pick the cords back up.
The psalm does not say nobody at the gathering is holding anything tight. It records what the rulers say about the chains and cords.
The psalm does not say nobody is hiding in heaven or call God the calmest one in the psalm. It goes on to speak of His anger and fury.
The psalm does not say what the kings thought about their gathering or that God had already answered them at that point.
The psalm says God has installed His King, but does not say it happened before the kings finished their gathering.
The reference to a flood in another Bible story needs a Scripture reference.
The reference to fire coming down from heaven in another Bible scene needs a Scripture reference.
The extent of the Son's promised possession does not establish how long He will rule. The explanation implies that it bears on the duration.
The verse tells the kings to serve the LORD with fear; it does not say they are being directed to seek help from Him.
The psalm does not say the kings' rebellion started when they planned to break the chains.
The oven-mitt joke makes light of God's wrath, rather than keeping humor on the human side of the moment.
